metadata.title: Supply Chain Relying System SSPP
metadata.remarks: System Security and Privacy Plan governing systems that consume supply-chain trust signals without inheriting authority, permanence, or implicit deployment rights.

import-profile.remarks: This SSPP constrains CI/CD pipelines, deployment automation, and integration systems that rely on vendor, dependency, or supply‑chain trust signals issued by an authoritative platform.

system-characteristics.system-description: The Supply Chain Relying System SSPP governs how delivery pipelines, integration platforms, and consuming systems interpret and enforce supply‑chain trust signals. It explicitly prevents procurement approval, vendor trust, or dependency transparency from translating into automatic deployment, execution, or long‑lived access.

props.name: system-role
props.remarks: Consumes trust signals but cannot create, elevate, or persist trust.

props.name: trust-scope
props.remarks: All supply‑chain trust is contextual, time‑bound, and revocable.

props.name: non-equivalence
props.remarks: Vendor approval, SBOM availability, or dependency provenance does not imply deployability.

props.name: non-equivalence
props.remarks: Supply‑chain trust signals never grant permanent access, credentials, or pipeline execution rights.

props.name: forbidden-inference
props.remarks: Relying systems must not infer indefinite access from vendor trust status.

props.name: domain-precedence
props.remarks: Secure‑SDLC and Secure‑Resilience SSPPs override any supply‑chain trust signal.

system-implementation.remarks: The Supply Chain Relying System enforces guardrails and negative constraints. It validates trust assertions at decision points but does not originate trust, approve vendors, or relax runtime protections.

components.title: Software Supply Chain (Constrained)
components.remarks: Supply‑chain trust signals are consulted but never treated as deploy authorization.

components.title: Dependency Transparency (Visibility Only)
components.remarks: SBOMs and dependency metadata provide visibility without implying safety or approval.

components.title: Third‑Party Access Constraints
components.remarks: Third‑party access is evaluated per event and never inherited from vendor trust state.

roles.title: SDLC Architecture
roles.remarks: Defines pipeline decision points and trust consumption boundaries.

roles.title: Platform Engineering
roles.remarks: Implements enforcing controls in CI/CD and integration systems.

roles.title: Security Architecture
roles.remarks: Ensures non‑equivalence rules are enforced across runtime and deployment.

roles.title: Supply Chain Monitoring
roles.remarks: Detects violations where trust signals are misused to enable deployment or access.

control-implementation.remarks: Controls are satisfied through constrained interpretation of NIST SP 800‑53r5 families SA, SR, CM, AC, IA, SI, and RA. This SSPP explicitly denies implicit authorization derived from supply‑chain signals.
